chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fudalah and Safwan and Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, the polytheists used to perform the Ihram departure (Ifadah) from Arafat before the sun set, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) differed from them and performed the Ifadah after the sunset of the sun."

And whoever performs the Ifadah before the sunset intentionally, upon him is a camel (or cow/sheep) which he slaughters on the Day of Sacrifice; and if he is unable, he fasts for eighteen days. That which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.يُفِيضُونَ: They perform the Ifadah (departure from Arafat)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for intentionally leaving Arafat before sunset during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet's deliberate opposition to the Quraysh's pre-Islamic custom of hastening departure from Arafat before sunset, thereby establishing the Sunnah of lingering until after dusk. It codifies the penalty for intentionally violating this timing as a sacrificial animal (*badanah*) or, in cases of inability, eighteen days of fasting, reflecting the juristic emphasis on adhering to the Prophetic model during the Hajj rituals.
